cases.title: Default Telemetry Behind a "No Telemetry" Homepage Promise
cases.summary: While its homepage promised "No telemetry. Unless you opt in. Full stop.", T3 Code enabled default PostHog tracking, routed raw copies through closed-source `ingest.t3.codes`, hashed external `~/.codex` and `~/.claude.json` credentials, and rejected four community opt-out PRs.
cases.claimHtml:
• The T3 Code homepage prominently promised: "No telemetry / Unless you opt in. Full stop."
  • Presented publicly as a privacy-first, open-source local AI coding client.
cases.evidenceHtml:
• Default tracking shipped under the "No telemetry" pledge (PR #174 → 3bdaa6e1): On March 6, 2026, PR #174 enabled default-on PostHog analytics with no consent dialog, no settings UI toggle, and no telemetry documentation. Over three months later, on June 18, commit 3bdaa6e1 silently deleted the "No telemetry" homepage promise during a redesign with zero user notice.
  • Closed-source first-party retention (PR #15028): In October 2026, telemetry batches (FLUSH_INTERVAL_MS = 10_000) were routed through T3's closed-source endpoint https://ingest.t3.codes/. Line 1 of AnalyticsService.ts confirms the server retains a raw copy of every event before forwarding to PostHog.
  • Cross-tool credential reading & unsalted SHA-256 (PR #21506): Baseline 9d3195b4 Identify.ts read ~/.codex/auth.json (decoding OpenAI's user_id JWT claim) and ~/.claude.json (oauthAccount.accountUuid) alongside T3 Connect user IDs, computing unsalted SHA-256 digests (telemetryId.ts) to link separate machines back to one person. Because T3 holds plaintext Clerk IDs, unsalted digests reverse deterministically.
  • Granular usage capture: ProviderUsageAnalytics.ts and FeatureUsage.ts reported providers, custom models, reasoning effort, permission mode, token counts, project/thread counts, OS/WSL metadata, and 35 distinct UI/command actions.
  • Four community opt-out PRs rejected: On June 23, maintainer Julius closed Issue #1397 (not planned): "We will not make this easier to opt out of, it is crucial for us to know how many users we have." Issue #4123 was closed silently, and four community opt-out PRs (#13458, #16763, #21248, #27077 — 147 passing tests, bot-approved) were rejected as unwanted.

cases.title: Fake SQLite Thread Deletion (41.6 GB Bloat) & 5-Second Full-OS Process Scanning
cases.summary: Clicking "permanently delete" left full conversation history intact inside `statev2.sqlite` (bloating local disks to 41.6 GB), while a background Rust monitor scanned every OS process and full command line every 5 seconds with zero opt-out.
cases.claimHtml:
• The sidebar deletion confirmation dialog (useThreadActionMenu.ts) explicitly told users: "This permanently clears conversation history for this thread."
  • T3 Code was marketed as a clean, fast local coding workspace.
cases.evidenceHtml:
• Fake permanent deletion (Issue #17845, #28903): At baseline 9d3195b4, deleting a thread only appended a "thread.deleted" event to statev2.sqlite while leaving prior messages, tool outputs, and reasoning traces intact on disk. Users documented statev2.sqlite ballooning to 25.9 GB in 3 weeks (90% "deleted" threads), 41.6 GB in 6 weeks, and 33 GB in 7 weeks.
  • Full-machine process & command-line scanning (Issue #11222, PR #41889): Background helper t3-resource-monitor (native/resource-monitor/src/main.rs) ran ProcessesToUpdate::All with with_cmd(UpdateKind::Always) every 5 seconds even with diagnostics closed — holding 280–300 persistent handles across 440+ unrelated apps/games on Windows. On November 24, PR #41889 confirmed diagnostics captured full process command lines (often carrying plaintext API keys, database passwords, and tokens) into snapshots and telemetry.
  • Corporate hostname leaks & mandatory startup fetch: Frontend favicon requests leaked internal hostnames (such as devbox.localdomain) to Google's favicon service (PR #16950, PR #32657), while server startup unconditionally fetched compatibility manifests from raw.githubusercontent.com with no opt-out (Issue #36479).
  • Severe quota burn & power bugs: Driving Claude via Agent SDK burned 5-hour quotas at 1.7x normal speed (Issue #7338, Issue #24649, 81 comments), while GPU regressions drew up to 136x comparable Electron power — pinning a MacBook GPU at 60W (78-minute battery drain) and 18W after closing the web tab (Issue #3143, Issue #40581).
cases.statusHtml:
• Partially patched: PR #42119 added asynchronous thread-content.purge (closing #17845), and PR #42577 narrowed Windows process-monitor reads.
  • Still open: Deleted source threads still keep history while referenced by live forks, pending merge_back, or live subagents; tombstone rows stay in SQLite and reclaiming disk space still requires offline VACUUM; Linux and macOS keep ProcessesToUpdate::All discovery, and PR #41889 remains open.

cases.title: Google Antigravity Header Spoofing, Fake `SSH_CONNECTION` & 3-Minute Account Bans
cases.summary: Despite guaranteeing ToS compliance in its FAQ, T3 Code extracts OS keyring credentials, spoofs Google internal headers (`antigravity/hub/2.24.0`) against `v1internal`, and injects fake `SSH_CONNECTION` values — exposing personal Google subscriptions to rapid bans.
cases.claimHtml:
• docs/user/faq.md assured paying subscribers: "We work with all of the labs and T3 Code is within the TOS of Claude Code, Codex, and Google Antigravity... If it works in T3 Code, you can trust it is safe."
  • When banned users filed Issue #40713, a maintainer denied hitting Antigravity's backend or reusing tokens — and on X, @theo blamed third-party proxies ("Not with cliproxy right?").
cases.evidenceHtml:
• OS credential extraction & spoofed v1internal calls: antigravityUsageLimits.ts extracts Google OAuth tokens from local files, @napi-rs/keyring, or Windows Credential Manager (CredReadW via ffi-rs on advapi32.dll), hardcodes antigravity/hub/2.24.0, and POSTs directly to Google's private v1internal endpoint. Google staff confirmed on the official forum that Section 6 of the Google Antigravity ToS prohibits third-party tools from extracting or reusing credentials to query backend endpoints directly.
  • Forged SSH_CONNECTION & cross-account leakage: antigravityAuthSupport.ts#L230-L236 injects a forged SSH_CONNECTION environment variable ("127.0.0.1 0 127.0.0.1 0") to trick Google's CLI out of OS keychain isolation into plaintext files. When Google updated its CLI on November 24, Issue #41973 confirmed prompts from Account A silently routed to Account B.
  • Fresh $20 account banned in 3 minutes (Issue #41536): A brand-new $20 Google AI subscription with zero proxies — using only T3-managed Antigravity — was banned on its very first message, 3 minutes after setup. Maintainers closed the issue as a duplicate without adding any user warning.
  • Native client & CLIProxyAPI spoofing: @theo personally merged PR #26876 masquerading as "zed", while merged PR #33800 wired cliproxyApi.ts hub polling with spoofed claude-code/2.1.273, grok-cli/1.0.77, and antigravityUserAgent headers.

cases.title: T3 Connect: Zero End-to-End Encryption & Plaintext TLS-Termination Gateway
cases.summary: Every prompt, source file, and terminal stream routed through T3 Connect terminates in plaintext inside T3-controlled infrastructure — with zero end-to-end encryption and default-off device approval.
cases.claimHtml:
• On November 24, @theo stated conversation data "lives on your machine. It never touches any of our servers" (2125191784859115766).
  • privacy-policy.astro (effectiveDate="2026-10-06") promises "encrypted network transport" without disclosing the absence of end-to-end encryption.
cases.evidenceHtml:
• Plaintext visibility inside T3's relay (ManagedEndpointProvider.ts): T3 Connect provisions Cloudflare Tunnels inside T3's own Cloudflare account (docs/internals/06_t3-connect.md). Transport TLS terminates at Cloudflare's edge with zero client-to-client payload encryption, meaning attaching a Cloudflare Workers Route exposes every prompt, file, and terminal stream in plaintext.
  • E2E encryption rejected as out of scope (Issue #32098): When developers requested mutual auth and end-to-end encryption, a maintainer closed Issue #32098 as too large a change; Discussions #21286 and #37831 went unanswered. On November 25, @theo declared E2E encryption impossible (2125370330244128924).
  • Migration to T3-operated OVH Caddy gateway (PR #32945): After Cloudflare Tunnel bills reached $25,000/month, @theo opened PR #32945 to move onto a T3-rented OVH Hillsboro server (gw.t3coderelay.com), where T3's own Caddy instance terminates TLS and forwards plaintext over a Unix socket to a Go yamux proxy — still without E2E encryption.
  • Default-off device approval (PR #36419, settings.ts): requireConnectDeviceApproval still defaults to false in packages/contracts/src/settings.ts (lines 1424–1426). As SECURITY.md acknowledges, a compromised cloud account or leaked relay signing key grants shell-equivalent host access.
cases.statusHtml: • Still open: PR #42311 added sign-in notifications, but T3 Connect still has zero end-to-end encryption, requireConnectDeviceApproval remains false by default, and privacy-policy.astro remains unchanged since 2026-10-06.

cases.title: The 77,000-Star Funnel: 30s-Idle Host-Credential Starring & Unfixed Arbitrary-Repo Bug
cases.summary: Six months after condemning GitHub stars as a way "to trick VCs into investing", @theo self-merged an in-app 30-second-idle toast that fires `PUT user/starred/...` using host GitHub credentials — catapulting the repo from 30k to 77k stars (with ~129 watchers) while leaving an arbitrary-repo starring bug unfixed.
cases.claimHtml:
• On April 26, 2026, @theo published "Github has a fake star problem", writing that GitHub stars had become "mostly a way for companies to trick VCs into investing" (2048122499834036340).
  • On November 24 at 74.6k stars, he claimed he "completely missed crossing 70k" (2124992724223029538).
cases.evidenceHtml:
• 10× daily star cliff via in-app idle toast (PR #27832, #29922, #29987): After taking 8+ months to reach 30,000 stars, @theo self-authored and self-merged PR #27832 on October 30 adding a star toast after 5 sent prompts (PROMPTS_BEFORE_ASKING = 5), immediately 10×'ing daily stars (+3,094 stars/day on GitHub Trending). On November 3, PR #29922 and PR #29987 added 30-second window idle detection (IDLE_MS = 30_000) while users wait on AI turns and replaced the browser redirect with a server-side sourceControl.star RPC firing PUT user/starred/pingdotgg/t3code directly through the host server's gh CLI / GH_TOKEN credentials, followed by 160-particle confetti.
  • Bypassed review & shared-host account opacity: Macroscope flagged PR #29922 as Needs Human Approval over browser-user vs. server-credential mismatch; @theo self-merged anyway. On shared or remote hosts, clicking Star silently stars the repo using whoever owns the server's GitHub credentials without telling the user which account was used.
  • Unfixed arbitrary-repo starring bug (driver.ts#L60-L99): On November 6, developer zhilsinger filed Request changes pointing out that packages/source-control-github/src/server/driver.ts#L60-L99 accepts any owner/repo string without pinning pingdotgg/t3code — letting any client with source-control:write star arbitrary GitHub repositories using host credentials.
// packages/source-control-github/src/server/driver.ts (lines 60–66, 90–96)
const starredPath = (repository: string) => {
  const segments = repository.split("/");
  return segments.length === 2 && segments.every((segment) => !["", ".", ".."].includes(segment))
    ? `user/starred/${segments.map(encodeURIComponent).join("/")}`
    : undefined;
};

cases.title: `ca81b7b9` Critical Auth & Repo Execution Audit: 30-Day Plaintext LAN Shell, Unrevocable Tokens & `SSH_AUTH_SOCK` Exposure
cases.summary: Line-by-line verification of latest `main` HEAD (`ca81b7b9`, Nov 25 14:49 CST) confirmed five active security and reliability flaws: 30-day plaintext `--lan` shell cookies with missing-`Origin` bypass, unrevocable 30-day Bearer tokens, replayable `?wsTicket=` URLs, `isIPv4` killing `::1` tunnels, and untrusted repositories executing hooks/submodules with inherited `SSH_AUTH_SOCK` and `GITHUB_TOKEN`.
cases.claimHtml:
• After the November 24–25 overnight patching blitz, T3 Code was presented as cleaned up and safe for daily engineering use.
  • SECURITY.md defines a default session as full OS-user shell control, while claiming local/LAN boundaries are properly managed.
cases.evidenceHtml:
Verified directly against upstream commit ca81b7b9:

  • 1. 30-day plaintext --lan shell cookies + missing-Origin bypass: SessionStore.ts#L492-L493 sets a 30-day default session TTL (equivalent to full OS shell access per SECURITY.md). PR #37042 added the Secure attribute only for https:, leaving t3 up --lan HTTP cookies transmitted in cleartext (http.ts#L215-L221). Worse, EnvironmentAuth.ts#L798-L806 returns true whenever Origin is omitted — so anyone sniffing a single LAN packet can replay the cookie from a non-browser script without Origin and hold 30-day host shell access silently.
  • 2. Unrevocable 30-day non-DPoP Bearer tokens & no /logout route: /oauth/token only shortens lifetime to 1 hour when DPoP proof is supplied; otherwise it issues an unbound 30-day Bearer token (EnvironmentAuth.ts#L1175-L1186). The HTTP contract defines zero /logout endpoint (environmentHttp.ts#L595-L679), and revokeClientSession explicitly blocks self-revocation with current_session_revoke_not_allowed (EnvironmentAuth.ts#L1506-L1511).
  • 3. Replayable 5-minute ?wsTicket= URL tokens: WebSocket tickets travel in query strings (?wsTicket=, landing in proxy/access logs) with a 5-minute TTL. SessionStore.ts#L1086-L1156 checks signature, expiry, audience, and revocation with no single-use jti replay store — allowing unlimited replays of Bearer RPC and all media tickets within 5 minutes (EnvironmentAuth.ts#L1553-L1622).
  • 4. Untrusted repositories running with full SSH_AUTH_SOCK & GITHUB_TOKEN: Worktree setup automatically runs git submodule update --init --recursive whenever .gitmodules exists (GitVcsDriverCore.ts#L6144-L6205); VcsProcess.ts#L145-L157 omits a global core.hooksPath=/dev/null guard; and ClaudeAdapterV2.ts#L5982-L5985 runs .claude/settings.json SessionStart hooks synchronously — all inheriting full host process.env including GITHUB_TOKEN and SSH_AUTH_SOCK (whose blast radius spans every remote repo and production server your SSH agent can sign for).
  • 5. isIPv4 silently destroying ::1 loopback tunnels: startupAccess.ts#L71-L108 adds ::1 to the loopback allowlist on line 39, then calls NodeNet.isIPv4 on line 73 — misclassifying IPv6 loopback Tailscale Serve and T3 Connect sockets as external traffic and calling socket.destroy().
